== Biography ==
'''James Glasgow''' was surgeon of His Majesty’s sloop ''Swift'' at Sheerness when he made his will on 15 June 1716. His will was proved at London on 21 August 1719, so his death falls after the will and by probate; no exact death day or place is established.<ref name="SwiftWill1716">The National Archives, [https://discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/details/r/D682397 PROB 11/569/479], will of James Glasgow, surgeon of HMS sloop Swift at Sheerness, 15 June 1716, proved 21 August 1719; original PDF pp.1–2 visually checked 12 November 2026. Uncertain words and cancelled text are not treated as verified names.</ref>

He expressly called '''Isabell Duff''' his mother and '''Jean''' his sister. He mentioned property in North Britain, particularly Edinburgh, and made provision for the poor of Lady Yester’s parish there. Surgeon John Barclay was his executor.<ref name="SwiftWill1716" />

The later Edinburgh testament index records a surgeon James as son of James Glasgow, weaver and burgess of Edinburgh, by Isobel Duff. The father is confidently identified with [[Glasgow-2682|James Glasgow]], and mother with [[Duffe-18|Isobell/Elizabeth Duffe]], each retained at 95% subjective confidence. The original will confirms the named maternal role and specific surgeon/Swift/Sheerness identity; it does not supply a legible father’s name. [[Glasgow-3088|Jean Glasgow]], indexed 13 April 1677 at Edinburgh to James Glasgow and Issobell Duff, is a strong sister candidate, not a proved adult identity. The 1733 index dates do not show the surgeon living in 1733. Saltoun remains an occupational-source association and uncertain birthplace.

== Research Notes ==
The original will and its death bound supersede earlier no-family-known or alive-in-1733 interpretations. The late newspaper passages below are retained as research history; the surgeon’s death by 21 August 1719 excludes identification with their living subjects. The 1696 apprentice [[Glasgow-4114]] and 1679/1680 child profiles remain separate. Swift is directly read in the English will; Surf remains the published Scottish index variant. The Scottish originals and Services of Heirs entry remain uninspected. The older Edinburgh index argument is preserved below with its citation, under its actual administrative date.

=== Earlier printed-index argument — superseded only where noted ===
'''James Glasgow''' of Saltoun, East Lothian, was a mariner. A derivative indexed under 1733 describes him as surgeon of the ''Swift'' of Sheerness in a list of Lothians mariners.<ref name="FMP1" /> The entry places him at Saltoun and records his occupation, but gives no age, family or later life, so his birth is placed before 1733 and Saltoun is inferred from the record rather than independently stated.

The Edinburgh testament index dated 3 February 1733 names James Glasgow, weaver and burgess of Edinburgh, and James Glasgow, surgeon on board H.M. sloop “Surf,” his son by the deceased Isobel Duff. A separate entry dated 4 April 1733 describes Isobel Duff as the weaver’s relict.<ref name="EdinburghSurgeon1733">Francis J. Grant (ed.), The Commissariot Record of Edinburgh, Register of Testaments, Part III, Volumes81–131,1701–1800 (Edinburgh: Scottish Record Society,1899), [https://www.electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso03scotuoft.pdf#page=116 printed p.106/PDF p.116], entry3February1733; [https://www.electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso03scotuoft.pdf#page=91 printed p.81/PDF p.91], Isobel Duff entry4April1733. Printed pages inspected30October2026; original testaments not inspected. These are index dates, not recorded death dates.</ref> The named couple and the father’s occupation identify the existing [[Glasgow-2682|James Glasgow]] and [[Duffe-18|Isobell/Elizabeth Duffe]] household. The uncommon name and surgical occupation make [[Glasgow-4124|James Glasgow]], the Saltoun surgeon of the “Swift of Sheerness,” a confident identification with this son. His father and mother are each assessed at95% subjective confidence; both depend on that same identity inference.

“Surf” is the literal printed reading in Grant, while the Dobson/Findmypast transcript reads “Swift.” The vessel discrepancy remains unresolved. Dobson cites SRO.S/H (Services of Heirs); that original and the original1733testament have not been inspected. The register dates are not death dates. That 30 October review made no vital change; the newly inspected will now supplies the 1716–1719 death bounds. The surgeon is not identified with the1696apothecary apprentice [[Glasgow-4114|James Glasgow]] or with either childhood James, [[Glasgow-3103]] and [[Glasgow-3368]]. The apprentice’s father82% and mother72%, James-2682’s own father61% and older-weaver identity70% remain distinct assessments.

=== Retained earlier research notes ===
The Dobson occupational transcript itself names no relative. The separate1733testament-index family clause below supports identifying his parents, while the later newspaper comparisons remain unproved.

=== Possible Captain Glasgow, brig Ann and Larne passenger reports, 1788 ===
The brig Ann is listed inward with Glasgow as master and Larne as origin.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/604128637/ The Columbian Herald, or, The Independent Courier of North-America, 1788-01-28, p.2].</ref>

The brig Ann, Captain Glasgow, is reported arriving from Larne after a tedious passage with near 200 passengers in good health; the report praises the captain’s humane and generous behaviour.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1034014648/ The Pennsylvania Journal, or, Weekly Advertiser, 1788-02-13, p.2].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39957255/ The Independent Gazetteer, 1788-02-16, p.2].</ref>

The brig Ann is listed cleared out with Glasgow as master and Georgetown as destination.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/604128661/ The Columbian Herald, or, The Independent Courier of North-America, 1788-02-18, p.2].</ref>

The passenger reports repeat one notice. The inward and outward entries may concern the same captain, but none gives his forename or family; Larne is the voyage origin, not a recorded birthplace.

This may concern [[Glasgow-4124]]. Prior research reports a 1733 mariners-list surgeon; no later life, brig Ann or Larne connection. No James forename in the 1788 notices.

=== Possible James Glascow, Fogs Manor postal addressee ===
James Glascow, Fogs Manor, is listed among letters remaining in the Philadelphia post office.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39395391/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1757-04-07, p.1].</ref>

Fogs Manor is the printed address qualifier. A neighbouring "Phil. Co." in a separate alphabetic column is not this man’s address. The list states no occupation, so it does not identify him as the later Greenwich Packet master.

This may concern [[Glasgow-4124]]. Before-1733 James Glasgow mariner/surgeon of Swift of Sheerness is chronologically compatible and occupationally relevant. The ship, route, region, and 44-year documentary gap provide no demonstrated identity link. The postal record states no occupation.

=== Possible James Glascow, master of Greenwich Packet ===
Greenwich Packet: James Glascow, master; James Young, owner; from Philadelphia to Winyew, Carolina; with rum, bread, flour and porter.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/34421452/ The Public Advertiser, 1777-05-14, p.2].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/396765804/ The Ipswich Journal, 1777-05-17, p.1].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/971522063/ The Gloucester Journal, 1777-05-19, p.1].</ref>

James Young is the separate vessel owner, not another form of the master’s name. Three issues repeat one voyage report. Neither the route nor the cargo establishes the master’s family or identifies him with the 1757 Fogs Manor addressee.

This may concern [[Glasgow-4124]]. Before-1733 James Glasgow mariner/surgeon of Swift of Sheerness is chronologically compatible and occupationally relevant. The ship, route, region, and 44-year documentary gap provide no demonstrated identity link.

=== Possible James Glasgow, Edinburgh game certificate, 1789 ===
James Glasgow, Esq., Edinburgh, appears in the Mid-Lothian game-duty list of certificates issued since 8 September 1789.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/601822968/ The Edinburgh Advertiser, 1789-12-11, p.8].</ref>

The list gives an Edinburgh designation but no age or relatives; it is not evidence of a military or maritime career.

This may concern [[Glasgow-4124]]. Birth before 1733, uncertain, Saltoun, East Lothian; death not recorded. Chronology and Scottish locality make this a possible candidate, but no evidence links him to the Edinburgh game-certificate entry or establishes Esq status.
